rurima has no relationship with docker, for now, it just provides a way to pull the image and parse the config from dockerhub. 
In the future, it might add more functions, to make it a partial replacement of docker, but as it will not support OCI or docker command-line arguments, it will not be a full replacement of docker and might need the user to solve problems in the container by themselves.
Thanks for reporting, du is only for showing the process when backing up a container, it should be an optional dependency but not must, I've fixed this.

If you are sure that your DNS config(/etc/resolv.conf) is correct, try running  this script inside the container: https://github.com/RuriOSS/daijin/blob/main/src%2Fshare%2Ffixup.sh
This might work for some Android devices.
And, for some old ping implementation, they need CAP_NET_RAW. You can grant it by adding `-k CAP_NET_RAW` argument, and don't forgot that this change need a restart (rurima r -U /path/to/container) of container to apply.

This is a bit weird, as CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE is already granted by default, port listening should not be denied. And also, as CAP_NET_RAW granted, ping should not be denied. I didn't get other users had such issue before.
You can try granting it full privilege by adding `-p` argument with the same steps, if it still doesn't work, please share me more information (device, android version, kernel version, how you created the container).
And for testing, if you can try exec `su - root` and then ping (to find if it's caused by missing setgroups() for root). And, if commands like curl that don't need any privileges work properly?

Thank you for your help. Using `su - root` inside the container made ping work, including connecting to external networks and running node. I also performed additional testing and confirmed that for my device, the `-k CAP_NET_RAW` and `-p` operations are unnecessary. Simply running the `fixup.sh` script followed by `su - root` resulted in everything functioning as expected. My device runs kernel 4.19.157 on Android 13.

```
#!/system/bin/sh

  echo "fake version"
